subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Proper way to add binary trait data for analysis

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Proper way to add binary trait data for analysis
parts:
I would encode the phenotype as 0/1 (0=unaffected, 1=affected). In scanone/scantwo/fitqtl/etc., use model="binary".

karl

On Feb 25, 2013, at 7:50 AM, Bruce Herron <cousin...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Karl and group
>
> We have been mapping seizure traits in BXD recombinant inbred mice as well as a confirmatory F2 cross and have had good results with our quantitative measures of phenotype (e.g. seizure susceptibility) using R/qtl. However, another aspect of this model is the progression of the seizure type in mice to shift from a forebrain seizure to a brainstem seizure over multiple seizures that also has a genetic component (only happens in the B6 parental lines). We would like to use this binary trait to map QTL associated with the shift, but are struggling with the best way to enter the data into our analysis. Can anyone provide suggestions or examples of the proper way to perform binary complex trait analysis in R/qtl?
>
> Greatly appreciate your input
>
> Bruce
>

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Proper way to add binary trait data for analysis
parts:
The best thing to do would be to implement your own version of Haley-Knott regression with a generalized linear model (the glm in function in R).

karl


On Feb 25, 2013, at 12:33 PM, Bruce Herron <bhe...@wadsworth.org> wrote:

> Thanks Karl
>
> this should work well for the F2 cross, but for the BXD data set we
> have tested at least 4 individuals for each BXD line. We had
> considered using a scoring system of 1 and -1 and then taking the
> average of each line, but then we are no longer dealing with a binary
> trait, yet still not a normal distribution.
>
> Bruce
